parts.label: (a)
parts.stem:
The table shows information about some of the elements in the third period.

| element | $\text{Na}$ | $\text{Mg}$ | $\text{Al}$ | $\text{P}$ | $\text{S}$ | $\text{Cl}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| atomic radius/nm | $0.186$ | $0.160$ | $0.143$ | $0.110$ | $0.104$ | $0.099$ |
| radius of most common ion/nm | $0.095$ | $0.065$ | $0.050$ | $0.212$ | $0.184$ | $0.181$ |
| maximum oxidation number of the element in its compounds | $+1$ |  |  |  |  | $+7$ |

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Complete the table to show the maximum oxidation number of each element in its compounds.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why the atomic radius of elements in the third period decreases from $\text{Na}$ to $\text{Cl}$.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
The radius of the most common ion of Mg is much smaller than the radius of the most common ion of S.

Identify both ions and explain the difference in their radii.

parts.label: (b)
(b)(i)
parts.text: Write an equation to represent reaction 1, the formation of compound **A**.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Give **two** observations you could make in reaction 2.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Cerium is a lanthanoid metal that shows similar chemical reactions to some elements in the third period. Most of cerium's compounds contain $\text{Ce}^{3+}$ or $\text{Ce}^{4+}$ ions.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Cerium shows the same structure and bonding as a typical metal.

Draw a labelled diagram to show the structure and bonding in cerium.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Cerium(IV) oxide, $\text{CeO}_2$, is a ceramic.

Suggest **two** physical properties of cerium(IV) oxide.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.stem:
A naturally occurring sample of cerium contains only **four** isotopes. Data for **three** of the isotopes are shown in the table.

| isotope | $^{136}\text{Ce}$ | $^{138}\text{Ce}$ | $^{140}\text{Ce}$ | $^{142}\text{Ce}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| relative isotopic mass | $135.907$ | $137.906$ | $139.905$ | to be calculated |
| percentage abundance | $0.185$ | $0.251$ | $88.450$ | to be calculated |

The $A_{\text{r}}$ of the sample is $140.116$.

Use these data to calculate the **relative isotopic mass** of the fourth isotope in this sample of cerium.

Give your answer to **three** decimal places.
